描述_ZN: Porcelain jar with five links in green glaze, Eastern Han dynasty, 46.5 cm high, 6.4 cm in diameter, 16.5 cm in base diameter.　　The main body of the five-linked jar is in the form of a three-sectioned gourd. Glazed green to the abdomen, under which the glaze flows several ways. The upper abdomen is in the shape of a two-section gourd, around which four small jars are stacked. The waist of the jar is decorated with bears, turtles and lizards. The lower abdomen has four string lines. The tapered shin and flat bottom.　　Five linked jars were first fired in the Eastern Han Dynasty, mostly excavated in the Jiangnan area, is buried with the medieval vessels. In the early period, the shape of the vessel was simple, and there were few piles of plastic. Later, the decoration became more and more complex, with many figures and animals. By the Western Jin Dynasty, it evolved into a barn pot, which has high artistic value. The barn jar is the inheritance and change of the popular five-link jar burial in the Han Dynasty, mainly for the deceased in the other world to feed and clothe the soul to the greatest extent possible.
